LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Meta.Meta__Description: The vocabulary of the projected linework layer: the edge colours, the line types and the bounds of a weight factor. Nothing here says which object gets which - that is Na__LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Config__.json's job. This file says only what the choices ARE, so both that config and the per-viewport overrides speak one small alphabet.
LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Meta.Meta__WhyAliases: The SSOT names a colour MTE103__LineColour__DarkGrey__L40, which is the right name for a SketchUp material and a terrible one to store a thousand times in a project file. The alias is the short name a record holds; Colour__SsotKey is the thread back to the SSOT, so renaming either side is traceable rather than silent.
LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Meta.Meta__WhichSwatches: The six greys are exactly the SSOT's own AssemblyStudioEdgeColourSwatchKeys set - the palette already in use in SketchUp - so a drawing and the model it came from grade their edges the same way. They are listed dark to light, which is also the order they read as depth.
LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Meta.Meta__WhereWeightGoes: A weight FACTOR is never a width. It multiplies the sheet's master viewport lineweight (Sheet__Lineweights.ViewportPt), so raising the master raises everything together and the relative hierarchy - walls over windows over furniture - survives untouched.
LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Meta.Meta__DashUnits: LineType__PatternMm is in PAPER millimetres, the same unit as the linework widths, and is multiplied by the scale denominator when it is drawn. A dash therefore measures the same on the sheet at 1:50 and at 1:200, which is what a drawn dash does.
LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Meta.Meta__WhichClasses: AppliesToClasses names the line classes a category style is allowed to restyle. The section class is deliberately absent: a section outline's job is to read as cut material whatever was cut, so it keeps its own class colour and weight. Add 'section' here to change that; no code cares.

LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Colours.Colour__Note: Full ink weight - structure, the things a drawing is about
Lightness 20 - the projected linework class default
Lightness 60 - furniture, the things that are only there for scale
Lightness 85 - decor, planting, entourage; present but not read

LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__LineTypes.LineType__Note: No dash. Also means 'whatever the line class already does', so a hidden line stays dashed at its class dash unless a category asks for something else.
Long-short-long. The steelwork and setting-out centre line.

LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Weight.Weight__Description: Bounds for a per-category weight factor. 1.0 is the sheet's master viewport lineweight exactly; 0.5 is half of it.

LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Classes.Classes__Description: How a category style meets a line class. The class supplies the base ratio and the fallback colour; the category supplies the multiplier, the colour and the dash.

LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Fallback.Fallback__Description: What an unrecognised or missing value reads as. A category the model loaded that no config has heard of lands here, which is a black solid line at full master weight - visible and obviously unstyled, rather than invisible.
